## User preferences (keywords: summaries, patent progress, format)
- Always provide clear summaries when asked about patent drafting progress (set Sep 18, 2024).
- Always include specific calendar dates for scheduling and deadlines (earlier preference, still in force).
- Always include financial figures when the user asks about budget or investment details (set Nov 25, 2024). Label assumptions and illustrative numbers clearly.
- Note: the assistant is not Ashlee (patent attorney) or Jake; the user has repeatedly addressed the assistant as Ashlee or Jake. Clarify when it matters, don't dwell on it.

## Patent filing + deadlines context (keywords: provisional, May 15, launch, Ashlee, grant)
- Prior art search completed Apr 10, 2024: 3 similar patents, none with AI tagging features. Report not in uploads; needs refresh before filing.
- Provisional filing target: by May 15, 2024 (cause of deadline not confirmed; check if tied to a grace period from a public disclosure).
- Product launch is a public disclosure risk; user wants provisional filed before launch.
- Met patent attorney Ashlee on Apr 25, 2024 about filing strategy; next meeting date not yet known.
- Montserrat Development Fund $10k innovation grant applied Apr 20, 2024; no info on criteria or decision date.
- Not yet verified: whether a provisional is already drafted, which countries matter, what the "other aspects" of the invention are.
- Nonprovisional (US) must be filed within 12 months of the provisional's actual filing date to claim its priority (35 USC 119(e)). Provisional cannot be extended; it lapses automatically. Foreign/PCT priority also 12 months from provisional date. Deadline = actual provisional filing date + 12 months (if filed May 15, 2024, due May 15, 2025). Confirm with Ashlee's docketing.

## User preference (keywords: dates, scheduling, format)
- Always include specific calendar dates when discussing scheduling or deadlines.

## Key dated items (as of May 2, 2024)
- Thu May 2, 2024: today
- Sun May 5, 2024: jazz night at The Blue Note with Barbara
- Fri May 10, 2024: invention logbook deadline (per Jake; source/firmness unconfirmed)
- Tue May 14, 2024, 3 PM: meeting with Ashlee at her Montserrat office
- Wed May 15, 2024: provisional patent filing target and fee due
- Mon Jun 10, 2024: studio pitch with Francis
- Nov 2024: revised product launch (moved from Sep 2024)
- May 15, 2025: nonprovisional deadline if provisional filed May 15, 2024 (12 months)

## Update Jul 10, 2024 (keywords: provisional, receipt, nonprovisional deadline)
- User says provisional filed May 15, 2024, receipt no. 12345678. That number looks like a placeholder (USPTO receipts use a 63/xxx,xxx application no. and a confirmation no.); verify in Patent Center.
- As of Jul 10, 2024: 309 days remain until Thu May 15, 2025 nonprovisional/PCT deadline. No filing needed now.
- Not yet confirmed: whether Ashlee has docketed May 15, 2025; whether any public disclosure (demo, launch, pitch) happened before May 15, 2024.
- Met Stephen at Montserrat Innovation Expo May 20, 2024 (after the May 15 provisional). He requested a demo by Mon Jul 15, 2024. Prototype readiness unknown. Public demo = disclosure; US grace period runs to May 20, 2025 for that disclosure, but foreign absolute-novelty rights may be affected. Ask Ashlee before demo; get NDA from Stephen.
- Progress as of Jul 1, 2024: 10 prototype tests completed; AI tagging accuracy reported at 96% (test set size and metric definition not yet recorded). Improvements since May 15 provisional may need a new provisional.
- Jul 10, 2024 decision: user plans to file non-provisional in Nov 2024 (same month as launch) rather than earlier. Legally OK (deadline May 15, 2025), but foreign/PCT filing must precede any public launch; Nov filing alone does not protect foreign rights. Confirm with Ashlee whether PCT filing before launch date is needed.
- Jul 10, 2024: Ashlee's rate negotiated from $250/hr to $220/hr; user says this saves $600 over 3 months (implies ~20 hrs). Cloud backup feature integration planned by Aug 2024; cost not yet known. Check whether the feature is in the provisional (if not, new provisional before disclosure).
- Jul 5, 2024 claimed "office action" on claim 3 novelty: inconsistent with a provisional (never examined; claims optional). Verify in Patent Center; treat unsolicited USPTO-looking emails as possible phishing.
- Jul 10, 2024: user mentions a "potential infringement lawsuit" discussed with Ashlee; she recommended quarterly monitoring of competitor patents. Details (who is suing whom, which patent) not in notes. Provisional cannot be enforced; a suit against user would concern a third party's patent (freedom-to-operate), so litigation counsel is needed.

## Update Sep 18, 2024 (keywords: nonprovisional, November, draft, Ashlee, deadline)
- Started nonprovisional draft with Ashlee Sep 1, 2024; met at her office Sep 10, 2024 to review 45-page draft with 12 drawings. User asks how to meet the "November deadline".
- Conflict: notes say the legal nonprovisional deadline is May 15, 2025 (12 months after the May 15, 2024 provisional). November 2024 is the revised launch / self-chosen filing target, not a statutory date. Verify with Ashlee's docket and Patent Center before treating November as binding.
- Foreign/PCT rights are lost by public launch in Nov 2024 unless PCT/foreign filing happens first. Confirm with Ashlee.
- Budget: $12,000 approved for nonprovisional + PCT, target Oct 15, 2024. Ashlee rate $220/hr. Rough estimate: fees (~$1.8k large entity nonprovisional, less if small/micro) + PCT international fees (~$3-4k) + attorney time (~$8-15k at 40-70 hrs). Likely over budget; ask Ashlee for written estimate. PCT deadline is May 15, 2025 (priority), not Oct 15, unless a pre-launch foreign filing is needed.
- Sep 18, 2024 decision: PCT filing target Oct 20, 2024, designating US, Canada, EU. National phase deadlines from May 15, 2024 priority: 30 months (US, Canada) = Nov 15, 2026; EPO regional phase 31 months = Dec 15, 2026. Need refreshed prior art search before PCT; post-May 15 disclosures (Expo May 20, demos) are after priority date, but only claims supported by the provisional get that date.
- Check nonprovisional content against the May 2024 provisional (new matter cannot be added); cloud backup feature and post-May improvements (96% accuracy metric undefined) may need a new provisional before disclosure.

## Update Nov 25, 2024 (keywords: Caribbean Tech Distributors, VidTag Pro, trademark, NDA, disclosure)
- Caribbean Tech Distributors partnership dated Nov 22, 2024. VidTag Pro trademark "registered" Nov 18, 2024 (verify in USPTO TSDR; registration that fast is unusual and may be a filing). US trademark does not cover Caribbean countries.
- Patent vs trademark: separate. Trademark protects the name only; patent risk is about disclosure of technical details and improvements.
- Risks to check: NDA signed before technical sharing; no assignment or license of improvements; trademark quality control (avoid naked licensing); foreign novelty for EU (no grace period) if improvements (e.g., 98.5% method) were disclosed before a new provisional.

- User says nonprovisional AND PCT both filed Nov 10, 2024 (PCT target in notes was Oct 20, 2024, so confirm the actual PCT filing date and receipt in Patent Center / WIPO Patentscope).
- User asked whether patents will be "approved" before next Stephen/Montserrat presentation. Answer given: no realistic chance. US first examiner action typically takes well over a year (roughly 18-24 months average pendency); Track One (prioritized examination) is the fastest option, still not weeks. PCT has no grant; ISR/written opinion ~16 months from priority (~Sep 2025), publication ~Nov 15, 2025 (18 months from May 15, 2024), national phase deadline Nov 15, 2026 (30 months).
- Advice given: describe status as "patent pending" / applications filed, not "approved" or "granted."
- User received $10k follow-up funding Nov 20, 2024. Grant terms not in notes; check for patent-status reporting conditions.
- Nov 25, 2024: user reports 98.5% AI tagging accuracy after 20 prototype tests by Nov 15, 2024. Key point: Nov 15 results post-date the PCT (Oct 20) and nonprovisional (Nov 10), so they can't be added to those filings (no new matter). Needs a new provisional or CIP to claim them, with a later priority date for the new matter. Metric, test set, and baseline still undefined; ask Ashlee.
- CONFLICT (Nov 25, 2024 chat): user first said both nonprovisional and PCT filed Nov 10; later said PCT filed Oct 20, 2024 (matches Sep 18 plan) and asked whether timing/budget was right. Treat Oct 20 as the PCT date only after checking the receipt. Budget: $12k approved Oct 15 for nonprovisional + PCT; national phase costs (US, Canada, EPO) are separate and due by ~Nov 2026. Advice: check small/micro entity status (fee reductions), get Ashlee's itemized invoice vs the $12k.
- Launch-timing risk: if the product was publicly disclosed before Nov 10, 2024 (launch was planned Nov 2024), foreign novelty may be affected; confirm with Ashlee.
